description: Static analysis and CI gate for AI code slop in JavaScript and TypeScript: cognitive complexity, god units, duplicate code, dead code, orphan features, SARIF and baselines.
rules: StopSlop detects structural code patterns; it does not determine whether code was written by a human or AI.
Run StopSlop without installing it with `npx stopslop .`. It requires Node.js ^20.19.0 or >=22.12.0 and analyzes JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript and TSX.
Exit code 0 means no unaccepted findings, 1 means findings were detected, and 2 means analysis or configuration failed.
Adopt an existing repository with `--baseline .stopslop-baseline.json --update-baseline`, commit that file, then use the same `--baseline` option in CI to reject only new findings.
A baseline changes the gate and reported findings but never lowers the full-repository slop score.
Use `--base <git-ref>` to compare against a Git revision without maintaining a baseline file. CI must fetch enough Git history to resolve that ref.
Report formats are text, json, sarif and shields. Use JSON for coding agents, SARIF for code scanning and shields for the binary `AI slop | clear` badge.
StopSlop works without configuration. Put optional overrides in `stopslop.json` and use `$schema: https://unpkg.com/stopslop/schema.json` for editor validation.
Use `--fast` only when intentionally skipping duplicate-code and dead-code analysis; it runs the AST checks for cognitive complexity and god units.
The Node API is ESM and typed: call `resolveConfig()` before `analyze()`, or call `loadConfig()` to read stopslop.json. The slop score always describes the complete analyzed repository.
Clone detection is powered by Clone Alert and dead-code analysis by Knip. Configure Knip only under the `knip` property in stopslop.json.
